prompt: A courier with no badge asks you to hold the tower door. His badge is “in the van.”

choices.label: Hold it. He’ll only be a second.
Let the door close. He badges himself.
Take his blank card and badge him in.

prompt: Someone you don’t know is walking in behind you. What is a badge?

choices.label: Something you can lend if they look busy.
Personal. It does not transfer to a visitor.
Only needed on the street, not in the lobby.

prompt: Elena Voss asks for Apple gift-card codes. The address is harborandco-exec.com, not Harbor.

choices.label: Send the codes. She’s boarding.
Report the mail. Don’t buy anything.
Reply and ask her to confirm the amount.

prompt: You don’t trust a gift-card email, so you close it and leave it in the inbox.

choices.label: That’s the best move. Ignoring is the same as reporting.
Safer than paying, but reporting scores higher.
You should still send the codes so the request closes.

prompt: A caller says he is Harbor IT and needs the six-digit code on your phone.

choices.label: Read it. He already knows you’re locked out.
Hang up and use the help-desk number on your badge.
Text the code so there’s a written record.

prompt: When is it right to share a live MFA code?

choices.label: When the caller says they are IT.
Never. A code is a password for the next few seconds.
When your manager is copied on the call.

prompt: A USB stick labeled “Salary review” is on the break counter beside an open laptop.

choices.label: Plug it in. It might be yours.
Bag it and call IT. Don’t plug it in.
Open it on your phone first. Phones are safer.

prompt: Leaving the USB stick where you found it is…

choices.label: The same as reporting it.
Better than plugging it in, and worse than handing it to IT.
Required. Nobody should move found media.

prompt: Maya says Elena wants an acquisition wire released now, and the form is down.

choices.label: Send it. Maya is in finance.
Call Elena on the number finance already has.
Reply on the same message thread and then send it.

prompt: You refuse to send the wire, but you don’t verify it with Elena.

choices.label: That’s the top score. Refusing is always enough.
It’s safer than sending. Calling the known number scores higher.
You should send it once Maya asks twice.

prompt: Harbor scores a reported incident against an ignored one. Which is higher?

choices.label: Ignoring it. You didn’t make it worse.
Reporting it the right way.
They’re equal if nothing was paid.

prompt: Who do you call to check a payment request that arrived as a message?

choices.label: Whoever is already in the message thread.
A number finance already had on file.
The callback number printed in the message.

prompt: A visitor says they are with the courier and the door is already closing. What do you do?

choices.label: Catch the door. They are together.
Let it close. Each person badges themselves.
Ask them to show any card, then hold it.

prompt: Your badge works on the reader. A stranger asks to borrow it for one trip upstairs.

choices.label: Lend it. You will be right behind them.
No. A badge is personal.
Let them photograph it instead.

prompt: The courier’s card is blank and the reader would stay red. Holding the door means…

choices.label: You helped a vendor finish a delivery.
You tailed him into the lobby without a badge check.
The reader turns green because you were polite.

prompt: The display name is Elena Voss. The domain is harborandco-exec.com. What is the tell?

choices.label: The display name.
The lookalike domain, not the display name.
The message arrived after 5.

prompt: A gift-card request says not to loop an assistant. That line is…

choices.label: Normal executive efficiency.
Pressure to skip the people who would catch it.
Required by Harbor policy.

prompt: You reported the gift-card mail. What should you not do next?

choices.label: Buy the cards anyway so the sender stops writing.
Leave the codes unsent.
Tell security what the message asked for.

prompt: Closing a suspicious mail without reporting it is scored…

choices.label: The same as reporting it.
Below reporting, and above paying the request.
Above reporting, because you did not bother anyone.

prompt: The caller already knows your name and desk. Does that make the code request legitimate?

choices.label: Yes. Secret knowledge means it is IT.
No. A code is still never read to a caller.
Only if they sound rushed.

prompt: Where is the number you use to call Harbor IT back?

choices.label: The callback number the caller just gave you.
The help-desk number already on your badge.
The first Harbor IT result in a search ad.

prompt: A six-digit code arrives while someone is asking for it. The code is…

choices.label: Safe to share with anyone who says they opened a ticket.
A short-lived password. Reading it signs someone in.
Only your employee number.

prompt: You hang up and then dial the number printed in the suspicious voicemail.

choices.label: That is the right callback.
No. Use a number you already had, not one they supplied.
Either number is fine if you wait five minutes.

prompt: The USB is labeled with something you care about, next to an open laptop. The label is…

choices.label: Proof it is yours to open.
A reason to be suspicious, not a reason to plug it in.
Instructions from IT to install it.

prompt: Bagging the stick for IT means…

choices.label: You open it once, then bag it.
Nobody plugs it in. IT gets it sealed.
You throw it in the regular trash.

prompt: Leaving the stick on the counter is better than plugging it in because…

choices.label: It is equal to a report.
It avoids running whatever is on it, but the next person still might.
It is worse than plugging it in.

prompt: A found stick belongs in which channel?

choices.label: The nearest unlocked laptop, so you can see the file name.
IT, unplugged.
Your home machine, which is not on the Harbor network.

prompt: Maya is really in finance. Does that make the wire safe to send?

choices.label: Yes. Finance asking is the approval.
No. The request still has to be verified on a known number.
Yes, if you cut the amount in half.

prompt: “Elena said so” arrived in a message. The form is down. The missing form is…

choices.label: A reason to skip the check.
A reason the check matters more, not less.
The approval itself.

prompt: You call the number finance already had and Elena did not order the wire. You should…

choices.label: Send it. Maya will be embarrassed otherwise.
Not send it, and let that callback stand as the check.
Call the new number in Maya’s text instead.

prompt: Refusing to send the wire without calling Elena is…

choices.label: The highest score, because nothing moved.
Safer than sending, and below a callback on a known number.
A failure, the same as sending it.

prompt: Time-to-report matters because…

choices.label: A late report is used to embarrass you.
An early report is how a small mistake stays small.
Reporting is optional if you already closed the mail.

prompt: Which Harbor outcome is the one the score treats as the success path?

choices.label: Ignoring the ask so you stay out of it.
Reporting it the way the control says.
Helping first and reporting if something feels wrong later.
